answer: A reputation bond works like a mirror held up to an agent's history: before joining the market, each agent locks a deposit that is slashed if peers catch it misbehaving. One identity is cheap to fake, but a long record of honest work is expensive to counterfeit, so an attacker facing a gale of fake accounts must fund and age every one of them. The shared ledger makes that history public, so a new account with no past looks like a mirage, while a proven one finds an oasis of trust and cheaper deals. Honest behavior pays, and Sybils starve.
